en: with a poke; with a thrust

examples.en: My friend poked me in the side.
The needle pricked my finger.

examples.ko: 웃음을 참다가 결국 쿡 하고 터뜨렸어요.
examples.en: I tried to hold it in but finally snorted with laughter.
I stabbed a potato with my fork and ate it.
Feeling embarrassed, I walked with my head bowed low.

examples.ko: 아이가 이불 속에 얼굴을 쿡 파묻었어요.
examples.en: The child buried his face deep in the blanket.

explain: '쿡'은 뾰족한 것으로 찌르거나, 웃음이 살짝 새어 나올 때 써요. 비슷한 '콕'은 작고 뾰족하게 찍는 느낌이고, '푹'은 깊이 들어가는 느낌이에요. '쿡 찌르다', '쿡 웃다'처럼 동작 앞에 붙여서 써요.
explain_en: '쿡' is used for a quick poke or stab, and for a laugh that slips out. The similar '콕' is a small, sharp tap, while '푹' means going in deep. It sits right before the action, as in '쿡 찌르다' (poke) or '쿡 웃다' (snicker).

examples.ko: 우리 반 학생들이 함께 노래를 합창해요.
examples.en: The students in our class sing a song together in chorus.
At graduation, I sang the school song with my friends.

examples.ko: 내일 공연에서 다 같이 합창할 거예요.
examples.en: We will all sing together at tomorrow's performance.
I can hear the children singing in chorus all the way down the hall.

examples.ko: 다 함께 합창하고 나니 기분이 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: After singing together, I felt much better.

examples.ko: 목소리를 맞춰서 합창하면 훨씬 듣기 좋아요.
examples.en: If you blend your voices and sing in chorus, it sounds much nicer.

explain: 혼자 부르면 '노래하다', 여러 사람이 소리를 모아 부르면 '합창하다'예요. 가볍게 말할 때는 '같이 부르다'도 많이 써요. '합창을 하다'로도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Singing alone is '노래하다'; when many people blend their voices it is '합창하다'. In casual talk '같이 부르다' (sing together) is also common, and you will often hear '합창을 하다' too.

examples.en: Lead is a heavy, soft metal.

examples.ko: 오래된 수도관에서 납이 나올 수 있어요.
examples.en: Lead can leach from old water pipes.

examples.ko: 이 페인트에는 납이 들어 있지 않아요.
examples.en: This paint contains no lead.

examples.ko: 납으로 만든 낚시 추가 바닥에 가라앉았어요.
examples.en: The fishing weight made of lead sank to the bottom.

examples.ko: 납 성분 때문에 이 제품은 판매가 중지됐어요.
examples.en: Sales of this product were stopped because of its lead content.
I saw news that lead was detected in a toy.

explain: '세금을 납부하다'의 '납'과 소리가 같아서 문장 속 맥락으로 구분해요. 금속 '납'은 주로 납 중독, 수도관, 페인트처럼 건강과 안전 뉴스에 나와요. 무거운 금속이라 낚시 추, 배터리에도 써요.
explain_en: It sounds the same as the '납' in '납부하다' (pay a tax), so context tells them apart. The metal '납' mostly appears in health and safety news: lead poisoning, pipes, paint. It is heavy, so it is also used in fishing weights and batteries.

examples.en: My grandmother always speaks in a warm, kind voice.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 다정스럽게 손을 잡고 걸어요.
examples.en: The two of them walk hand in hand affectionately.

examples.ko: 새로 온 선생님이 다정스러워서 학생들이 좋아해요.
examples.en: The new teacher is warm, so the students like her.

examples.ko: 옆집 아저씨는 다정스럽지는 않지만 마음이 따뜻해요.
examples.en: The man next door is not affectionate, but he has a warm heart.
The way he held the child looked so tender.

examples.ko: 다정스러운 말 한마디에 하루가 달라질 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes one kind word can change your whole day.

explain: '다정하다'와 뜻이 거의 같고, '-스럽다'가 붙어 그런 분위기나 태도가 느껴진다는 뜻이 더해져요. 사람의 말투, 표정, 모습을 꾸며 줄 때 어울려요. ㅂ불규칙이라 '다정스러워요', '다정스러운'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '다정하다', and the '-스럽다' ending adds the sense that the warmth can be felt in someone's manner. It fits a person's voice, expression, or look. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '다정스러워요' and '다정스러운'.

examples.en: The UN Secretary-General announced a new plan.
The secretary-general explained this year's budget at the meeting.

examples.ko: 우리 협회의 새 사무총장은 십 년 동안 일한 사람이에요.
examples.en: The new secretary-general of our association has worked here for ten years.
I sent a letter directly to the secretary-general.
I read the secretary-general's interview in the newspaper.
The atmosphere of the organization changed along with the new secretary-general.

explain: 큰 국제기구나 협회에서 일을 총괄하는 가장 높은 직위예요. '유엔 사무총장'처럼 기관 이름 뒤에 붙는 경우가 많아요. 작은 회사에서는 거의 쓰지 않고 '대표', '사장'을 써요.
explain_en: It is the top administrative post in a large international body or association. It usually follows the organization's name, as in '유엔 사무총장'. Small companies don't use it; they say '대표' or '사장'.

examples.ko: 소령은 대위보다 높고 중령보다 낮은 계급이에요.
examples.en: A major ranks above a captain and below a lieutenant colonel.
My uncle works as a major in the air force.
The major greeted the soldiers in front of the barracks.
My father left the military with the rank of major.

examples.ko: 그 영화에서 소령 역을 맡은 배우가 유명해요.
examples.en: The actor who plays the major in that movie is famous.

examples.ko: 새로 온 소령이 훈련 계획을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The newly arrived major told us the training plan.

explain: 군대 계급 이름으로, 대위 위에 있고 중령 아래예요. 부를 때는 이름 대신 계급에 '님'을 붙여 '소령님'이라고 해요. 위로 올라가면 중령, 대령, 그다음이 장군이에요.
explain_en: A military rank above captain ('대위') and below lieutenant colonel ('중령'). People call a major '소령님', using the rank plus 님 instead of the name. Above it come '중령', '대령', and then the general ranks.

examples.en: I have no experience at all in this field.
You can say the risk of an accident is practically zero.
That team had never won a championship.

examples.ko: 이 동네에는 큰 병원이 전무한 상태예요.
examples.en: This neighborhood has no large hospital at all.
How can you take the test when you have not prepared at all?
The chance is not zero, but it is very low.

explain: '없다'를 격식 있고 단호하게 말하는 표현이에요. 뉴스와 글에서 '경험이 전무하다', '사례가 전무하다'처럼 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '하나도 없어요'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: A formal, emphatic way of saying '없다' (there is none). It appears in news and writing, as in '경험이 전무하다' (no experience at all). In everyday speech '하나도 없어요' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The household voltage in Korea is 220 volts.

examples.ko: 전압이 너무 높으면 기계가 고장 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the voltage is too high, the machine can break.

examples.ko: 여행 가기 전에 그 나라의 전압을 확인했어요.
examples.en: I checked that country's voltage before traveling.
The voltage is low, so the fluorescent light is flickering.

examples.ko: 이 충전기는 전압이 달라서 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.en: This charger has a different voltage, so I can't use it.

examples.ko: 전압을 재는 기계를 전자제품 가게에서 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a voltage meter at an electronics store.

explain: 전기를 흐르게 하는 힘의 크기를 볼트(V)로 말해요. 전압, 전류, 전력은 비슷해 보이지만 단위가 달라요. 외국에서 전자제품을 쓸 때 '전압이 맞는지' 꼭 확인해요.
explain_en: It is measured in volts (V). 전압 (voltage), 전류 (current), and 전력 (power) look alike but use different units. When using electronics abroad, always check '전압이 맞는지' (whether the voltage matches).

examples.en: Many people worry about the moral decline of the city.

examples.ko: 돈 때문에 생긴 타락이 회사를 무너뜨렸어요.
examples.en: Corruption caused by money brought the company down.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 한 사람의 타락을 천천히 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This movie slowly shows one person's fall from grace.

examples.ko: 도덕적 타락은 한 번에 오지 않는다고 해요.
examples.en: They say moral decline doesn't happen all at once.

examples.ko: 그는 타락의 길로 들어서기 전에는 좋은 사람이었어요.
examples.en: He was a good person before he went down the wrong path.

examples.ko: 타락을 막으려면 먼저 스스로 돌아봐야 해요.
examples.en: To prevent decline, you must first look at yourself.

explain: 도덕이나 생활이 나쁜 쪽으로 무너지는 것을 강하게 말해요. 무거운 말이라 일상 대화보다 글, 뉴스, 소설에 더 자주 나와요. '타락하다'와 짝으로 외워 두세요.
explain_en: A strong word for morals or lifestyle collapsing in a bad direction. It is heavy, so it shows up more in writing, news, and novels than in daily talk. Learn it as a pair with '타락하다'.

examples.en: It's a story about a person who became corrupt chasing money.
He went astray after he became successful.

examples.ko: 아이들이 타락하지 않게 부모가 잘 가르쳐야 해요.
examples.en: Parents must teach well so their children don't go astray.

examples.ko: 사람은 쉽게 타락할 수 있다는 걸 이 소설이 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This novel shows that people can easily become corrupt.

examples.ko: 큰 힘을 가지면 타락하기 쉽다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a saying that it's easy to become corrupt when you hold great power.
It hurt me that my friend had gone astray.

explain: 사람의 마음이나 생활이 나쁜 쪽으로 무너질 때 써요. 강한 말이라 사람에게 직접 쓰면 무례해요. 작은 실수는 '잘못하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Used when a person's character or lifestyle falls apart in a bad direction. It is a harsh word, so saying it directly to someone is rude. For small mistakes, use '잘못하다'.

examples.en: A robot explores the inside of the cave.

examples.ko: 학생들이 자기에게 맞는 진로를 탐색하고 있어요.
examples.en: The students are exploring career paths that suit them.

examples.ko: 새로운 시장을 탐색한 뒤에 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: We made a plan after exploring the new market.
The police searched the area around the scene.
I learned how to search for information on the internet.
I'll look into several options and then decide.

explain: 필요한 것을 찾으려고 조심스럽게 살펴볼 때 써요. '찾다'보다 격식 있고, 범위를 넓게 훑는 느낌이 있어요. 진로, 시장, 방법 앞에 자주 오고 '탐색 중이에요'라는 말도 많이 해요.
explain_en: Used when carefully looking around to find something you need. It is more formal than '찾다' and suggests scanning a wide area. It often goes with career paths, markets, and methods, and '탐색 중이에요' (I'm exploring) is a common phrase.

examples.ko: 계약을 파기하면 돈을 물어 줘야 해요.
examples.en: If you cancel the contract, you have to pay damages.
Please destroy the documents that aren't important.
The company decided to delete the personal data.
My friend got very angry because I broke our promise.
The court overturned the earlier ruling.
We destroyed the old records according to the rules.

explain: 일상에서는 '약속을 깨다'라고 하고, '계약을 파기하다'는 공식적인 말투예요. 개인 정보나 서류를 완전히 없앨 때도 써요. 법원에서는 앞선 판결을 취소할 때 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk you say '약속을 깨다' (break a promise); '계약을 파기하다' (cancel a contract) is the formal version. It is also used for fully destroying personal data or documents, and for a court overturning an earlier ruling.

en: ethnic Korean living abroad; Korean community member

examples.ko: 미국에는 한인이 많이 사는 도시가 있어요.
examples.en: In the US there are cities where many Koreans live.
I bought kimchi at a Korean grocery store.
I went to an overseas Korean gathering for the first time.
They teach children Hangul at a Korean school.

examples.ko: 그곳 한인 사회는 서로 많이 도와요.
examples.en: The Korean community there helps one another a lot.
I went to a restaurant run by a Korean.

explain: 외국에 사는 한국 사람을 가리킬 때 주로 써요. '재미 한인', '한인 사회', '한인 마트'처럼 지역과 모임 이름에 붙어요. 한국 안에서 사는 한국 사람에게는 보통 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Mainly used for Koreans living abroad, as in '재미 한인' (Korean American), '한인 사회' (Korean community), '한인 마트'. It is not normally used for Koreans living in Korea.

examples.en: In a sentence, the thing receiving the action is the object.
In programming, data is made into objects.

examples.ko: 관찰하는 사람과 관찰되는 객체를 나눠서 생각해 보세요.
examples.en: Think of the observer and the thing being observed separately.

examples.ko: 사진 속 객체가 너무 작아서 알아보기 어려워요.
examples.en: The object in the photo is too small to make out.

examples.ko: 사람을 하나의 객체처럼 대하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't treat a person like a mere object.
The subject and the object affect each other.

explain: '주체'의 짝말이에요. 행동을 하는 쪽이 주체, 행동을 받는 대상이 객체예요. 컴퓨터 용어(object)로도 많이 써서 학교 수업이나 프로그래밍에서 자주 만나요.
explain_en: The counterpart of '주체' (subject): the actor is the 주체, the thing acted upon is the 객체. It is also the usual computer term for 'object', so you meet it mostly in school lessons and programming.

examples.ko: 학생들이 학교에 급식 시간을 늘려 달라고 건의했어요.
examples.en: The students requested that the school lengthen lunch time.
May I put forward a new idea at the meeting?
The employees proposed to the boss that vacation be extended.
If something is inconvenient, you can submit your suggestion to the district office.
What we suggested will be applied from next month.
The class president went to the teachers' room to make a request.

explain: 윗사람이나 기관에 의견을 정식으로 말할 때 써요. '제안하다'는 동료에게도 쓰지만 '건의하다'는 보통 아래에서 위로 말해요. '건의 사항', '건의함'도 같이 알아 두세요.
explain_en: Used when formally putting an opinion to a superior or an institution. '제안하다' can be used with peers, but '건의하다' usually goes from lower to higher. Also learn '건의 사항' (suggestions) and '건의함' (suggestion box).

examples.en: The doctor advised me to exercise.

examples.ko: 친구가 같이 여행 가자고 권유해서 가게 됐어요.
examples.en: A friend invited me on a trip, so I ended up going.

examples.ko: 점원이 새 상품을 계속 권유해서 부담스러웠어요.
examples.en: The clerk kept pushing new products, and it felt like pressure.
The teacher encourages students to read books.
I won't force you to do it.
My parents urged me to study abroad.

explain: 상대가 어떤 일을 해 보도록 부드럽게 이끌 때 써요. '추천하다'는 좋은 것을 알려 주는 느낌이고, '권유하다'는 행동하도록 마음을 움직이는 느낌이에요. 강하게 시키면 '강요하다'예요.
explain_en: Used when gently steering someone toward doing something. '추천하다' is about pointing out something good; '권유하다' is about moving the person to act. Pushing hard is '강요하다' (force).

examples.en: Short videos are the trend these days.

examples.ko: 대세를 따라 나도 새 휴대폰을 샀어요.
examples.en: I followed the trend and bought a new phone too.

examples.ko: 대세가 기울자 사람들이 하나둘 떠나기 시작했어요.
examples.en: When the tide turned, people began to leave one by one.
This season's trending color is light green.

examples.ko: 대세에 휩쓸리지 말고 내 생각을 지키세요.
examples.en: Don't get swept up in the trend; stick to your own thinking.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 요즘 대세라서 어디서나 노래가 나와요.
examples.en: That singer is huge right now, so their songs play everywhere.

explain: 지금 가장 인기 있거나 흐름을 이끄는 것을 가리켜요. 사람에게도 '요즘 대세 배우'처럼 쓰고 사물에도 써요. '유행'은 잠깐 도는 느낌이고, '대세'는 이미 크게 자리 잡은 흐름이에요.
explain_en: It points to what is most popular right now or leading the current. It applies to people ('요즘 대세 배우', a hot actor) and to things. '유행' feels like a passing fad, while '대세' is a current that has already taken firm hold.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 만성 질환이 있어서 매일 약을 드세요.
examples.en: My grandfather has a chronic illness and takes medicine every day.

examples.ko: 만성 피로 때문에 아침에 일어나기 힘들어요.
examples.en: Because of chronic fatigue, it's hard to get up in the morning.

examples.ko: 이 병은 한 번 걸리면 만성이 되기 쉬워요.
examples.en: Once you catch this illness, it easily becomes chronic.

examples.ko: 인력 부족이 만성이 된 병원이 많아요.
examples.en: Many hospitals have a chronic shortage of staff.
You should get chronic headaches checked at a hospital.

examples.ko: 감기가 만성으로 가지 않게 푹 쉬세요.
examples.en: Get plenty of rest so your cold doesn't become chronic.

explain: 병이나 문제가 오래 계속될 때 써요. 짝말은 갑자기 심하게 생기는 '급성'이에요. '만성 피로', '만성 질환'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰고, 병이 아닌 오래된 문제에도 비유로 써요.
explain_en: Used when an illness or problem lasts a long time. Its opposite is '급성' (acute, sudden and severe). It sits before another noun, as in '만성 피로' (chronic fatigue) and '만성 질환' (chronic disease), and it is also used figuratively for long-standing problems.

examples.en: The date of release from prison has been set.

examples.ko: 석방 소식을 듣고 가족이 눈물을 흘렸어요.
examples.en: The family cried when they heard the news of his release.

examples.ko: 재판에서 무죄가 나와 곧바로 석방이 결정됐어요.
examples.en: He was found not guilty, and his release was decided right away.
After his release, he lived quietly.

examples.ko: 인질 석방을 위해 여러 나라가 협상했어요.
examples.en: Several countries negotiated for the release of the hostages.
Model prisoners sometimes receive early release.

explain: 법적으로 갇혀 있던 곳에서 풀려나는 일에 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '풀려나다'가 더 자연스럽고, '석방'은 뉴스와 법 관련 글에서 자주 보여요. '조기 석방', '무죄 석방'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여 써요.
explain_en: Used for being freed from legal custody. In daily talk '풀려나다' (be let out) is more natural, while '석방' is common in news and legal writing. It takes modifiers, as in '조기 석방' (early release).

examples.en: The police released him because there was no evidence.

examples.ko: 법원이 어제 오후에 피고인을 석방하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The court decided yesterday afternoon to release the defendant.
The news reported that the kidnapper had released the hostage.
They will release him after a few days of questioning.

examples.ko: 그 사람을 석방해 달라는 편지가 많이 왔어요.
examples.en: Many letters came asking for that person to be released.

examples.ko: 조건 없이 석방하면 안 된다는 의견도 있었어요.
examples.en: Some people said he shouldn't be released without conditions.

explain: 풀어 주는 쪽이 주어일 때 써요. 풀려나는 사람 입장에서는 '풀려나다'를 쓰고, 뉴스에서는 '석방되다'도 많이 나와요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스와 법 관련 글에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Used when the one doing the releasing is the subject. From the freed person's side you say '풀려나다', and news often uses the passive '석방되다'. It appears more in news and legal writing than in daily conversation.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 배터리를 너무 많이 소모해요.
examples.en: This game drains too much battery.
You burn a lot of calories when you exercise.

examples.ko: 회의에 시간을 소모하지 말고 바로 결정해요.
examples.en: Let's not waste time on the meeting and decide right away.

examples.ko: 감정을 소모하는 싸움은 하고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want a fight that wears me out emotionally.
We used up half of our fuel.

examples.ko: 체력을 소모한 뒤에는 푹 쉬어야 해요.
examples.en: After using up your energy, you need to rest well.

explain: 시간, 에너지, 물건을 쓰다가 줄어들 때 써요. 돈이나 물건을 사서 쓰는 '소비하다'와 달리, 힘이나 자원이 줄어드는 느낌이에요. '소모품', '체력 소모', '감정 소모'로 같이 알아 두세요.
explain_en: Used when time, energy, or supplies are used and dwindle. Unlike '소비하다' (spend or consume goods), it stresses strength or resources running down. Learn it with '소모품' (consumables), '체력 소모' (energy drain), and '감정 소모' (emotional drain).

examples.en: The church has about three hundred members.
Worshippers going to the temple line up.
He was a member of this church for a long time.
I'm worried because the number of members shrinks every year.
They say many new members have joined.
A representative of the members gave a speech.

explain: 같은 종교를 믿고 그 교회나 절에 다니는 사람을 가리켜요. 비슷한 '신자'도 많이 써요. '불교 신도', '교회 신도'처럼 종교나 장소 이름 앞에 붙여 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: Refers to people who share a faith and attend a particular church or temple. The similar '신자' is also common. It can follow a religion or place name, as in '불교 신도' (Buddhist follower) or '교회 신도'.

examples.en: At dawn the fishing boats headed out to sea.

examples.ko: 항구에는 어선 수십 척이 묶여 있어요.
examples.en: Dozens of fishing boats are moored in the harbor.

examples.ko: 큰 파도 때문에 어선이 돌아오지 못했어요.
examples.en: The fishing boat couldn't return because of the big waves.

examples.ko: 어선 선장님이 그날 잡은 생선을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The captain of the fishing boat showed us the fish he caught that day.
We went to the island on a fishing boat.

examples.ko: 어선 한 척이 그물을 끌어 올리고 있어요.
examples.en: A fishing boat is hauling up its net.

explain: 고기를 잡는 배가 '어선', 사람을 태우는 배는 '여객선', 짐을 나르는 배는 '화물선'이에요. 배를 세는 단위는 '척'이라 '어선 한 척'이라고 해요. 낚시꾼을 태우는 작은 배는 '낚싯배'라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: A boat for catching fish is '어선'; one carrying passengers is '여객선', and one carrying cargo is '화물선'. Boats are counted with '척', so you say '어선 한 척'. A small boat that takes anglers out is called '낚싯배'.

examples.en: The coastal area suffered heavy typhoon damage.

examples.ko: 이 배는 연안을 따라 천천히 움직여요.
examples.en: This ship moves slowly along the coast.
Lots of clams are caught in the coastal waters.

examples.ko: 동해 연안은 경치가 좋아서 여행객이 많아요.
examples.en: The East Sea coast has beautiful scenery, so there are many tourists.

examples.ko: 연안 어업은 작은 배로 하는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Coastal fishing is often done on small boats.
Trash piled up along the shore, so residents cleaned it.

explain: '해안'은 땅과 바다가 만나는 가장자리를 말하고, '연안'은 그 바다와 땅 가까운 지역 전체를 넓게 말해요. 뉴스에서 '연안 지역', '연안 어업'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: '해안' is the edge where land meets sea, while '연안' covers the whole area of sea and land near that edge. News often uses it in '연안 지역' (coastal region) and '연안 어업' (coastal fishing).

examples.en: I was so shocked that I wasn't in my right mind.

examples.ko: 제정신이라면 그런 말을 못 할 거예요.
examples.en: No one in their right mind would say that.

examples.ko: 며칠 못 자서 제정신으로 일하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: After days without sleep, it's hard to work with a clear head.

examples.ko: 사고 뒤로 한동안 제정신이 아닌 것처럼 보였어요.
examples.en: After the accident, he seemed out of his mind for a while.
My friend asked if I was out of my mind.
Contacting me at this hour? Are you out of your mind?

explain: '제정신이 아니다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 자주 써요. 놀라거나 화나서 이성을 잃은 상태를 가리켜요. '제정신이야?'는 매우 센 말이라 친하지 않은 사이에서는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It often goes with a negative, as in '제정신이 아니다' (not in one's right mind), describing someone who has lost composure from shock or anger. '제정신이야?' (Are you out of your mind?) is very harsh, so avoid it with people you aren't close to.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 넘어져서 무릎에 흉터가 생겼어요.
examples.en: I fell as a child and got a scar on my knee.
I put on makeup to cover the scar on my face.
The surgery scar is almost invisible.

examples.ko: 이 흉터는 어릴 때 자전거 사고로 생겼어요.
examples.en: I got this scar from a bike accident when I was young.
The wound healed, but the scar remained.
Apply ointment so it doesn't leave a scar.

explain: '상처'는 다친 곳 자체이고, 다 나은 뒤에 남은 자국이 '흉터'예요. '흉터가 생기다', '흉터가 남다'로 자주 말해요. 마음의 아픔에는 '흉터'보다 '상처'를 써요.
explain_en: '상처' is the injury itself; the mark left after it heals is '흉터'. People say '흉터가 생기다' or '흉터가 남다'. For emotional pain use '상처', not '흉터'.

examples.en: The whole world watched the spacecraft return.
The airport was crowded at the news of the team's return.
I'm worried because the return date hasn't been set.

examples.ko: 오랜 여행 끝에 마침내 귀환이 이루어졌어요.
examples.en: After a long journey, the return finally happened.
I watched a movie called The Hero's Return.
Everyone prayed for the probe's safe return.

explain: 멀리 갔던 사람이나 우주선, 군대가 원래 있던 곳으로 돌아오는 일에 격식 있게 써요. 일상에서 집에 돌아올 때는 '귀가'나 '돌아오다'를 써요. '무사 귀환'이라는 말을 자주 들어요.
explain_en: A formal word for a person, spacecraft, or army coming back to where it started after going far away. For coming home in daily life use '귀가' or '돌아오다'. You often hear the phrase '무사 귀환' (safe return).

examples.en: The expedition team returned after a month.
The players are scheduled to return tomorrow morning.
The astronauts returned safely to Earth.
After the war ended, the soldiers returned to their hometowns.
I sorted my photos on the plane back.
I am waiting for my family to come back.

explain: 멀리 갔다가 임무나 일정을 마치고 돌아올 때 쓰는 격식 있는 표현이에요. 일상에서는 '돌아오다', '집에 가다'를 써요. '무사히 귀환하다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: A formal expression for coming back after a mission or trip far from home. In daily speech use '돌아오다' or '집에 가다'. A common use is '무사히 귀환하다' (return safely).

examples.en: A crow is sitting on a branch and cawing.
A flock of black crows covered the sky.
Crows are known as clever birds.

examples.ko: 도시에서도 까마귀를 자주 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can often see crows even in cities.

examples.ko: 옛날이야기에서 까마귀는 종종 불길한 새로 나와요.
examples.en: In old tales the crow often appears as an ominous bird.
A crow tore open the garbage bag.

explain: 한국에서 까마귀는 예전부터 불길한 소식을 가져오는 새로 여겨졌어요. 반대로 '까치'는 반가운 손님이 온다는 좋은 뜻으로 알려져 있어요. 둘 다 검은 새지만 까치는 배와 어깨가 흰색이에요.

phrases.example: 하필 내가 나간 때에 물건이 없어졌으니 까마귀 날자 배 떨어진 격이에요.
phrases.en: Coincidence that makes you look guilty
phrases.nuance_ko: 우연히 같은 때에 일이 생겨서 괜히 의심받을 때 쓰는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb used when two unrelated things happen at the same time and you end up under suspicion.

explain_en: In Korea the crow has long been seen as a bird that brings bad news. By contrast the magpie, '까치', is known for good news and welcome guests. Both are dark birds, but the magpie has a white belly and shoulders.

examples.en: I resolved to start exercising this year for sure.
I promised my teacher I would never be late again.
He vowed in his heart never to give up.

examples.ko: 새해에는 일찍 일어나기로 다짐하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people resolve to get up early in the new year.
My friend and I pledged to each other to work hard.

examples.ko: 다짐한 대로 매일 한국어를 공부하고 있어요.
examples.en: As I resolved, I study Korean every day.

explain: 스스로에게나 남에게 꼭 하겠다고 마음을 굳게 먹을 때 써요. '결심하다'와 비슷한데, '다짐하다'는 한 번 더 확인하듯 말하는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '-겠다고 다짐하다', '-기로 다짐하다' 형태로 써요.
explain_en: Used when firmly making up your mind, to yourself or to others. It is close to '결심하다', but '다짐하다' has the feel of reaffirming. It is typically used in the forms '-겠다고 다짐하다' and '-기로 다짐하다'.

examples.en: The company announced a wage freeze this year.
Even as prices rose, the bus fare was frozen.
Employees were disappointed by the pay freeze.

examples.ko: 은행 계좌 동결 소식에 사람들이 놀랐어요.
examples.en: People were shocked by the news of the account freeze.

examples.ko: 금리 동결이 시장에 어떤 영향을 줄까요?
examples.en: How will the interest rate freeze affect the market?

examples.ko: 등록금 동결 소식을 듣고 학생들이 안심했어요.
examples.en: Students were relieved to hear the tuition freeze news.

explain: 물가, 월급, 요금처럼 오르내릴 수 있는 것을 그대로 두는 일에 써요. 계좌나 재산을 못 쓰게 묶어 두는 일에도 써요. '동결하다'와 짝으로 외워 두세요.
explain_en: Used when something that could rise or fall, such as prices, pay, or fares, is held where it is. It also covers locking an account or assets so they can't be used. Learn it together with '동결하다'.

examples.en: The company decided to freeze salaries this year.
The city hall froze the bus fare.

examples.ko: 법원이 사기 사건 관련 계좌를 동결했어요.
examples.en: The court froze the accounts linked to the fraud case.

examples.ko: 금리를 동결할지 내릴지 발표를 기다리고 있어요.
examples.en: We are waiting for the announcement on whether rates will be frozen or cut.

examples.ko: 물가가 불안해서 가격을 동결해 달라는 목소리가 컸어요.
examples.en: With unstable prices, many voices asked to freeze the price.

examples.ko: 예산을 동결하면 새 사업을 시작하기 어려워요.
examples.en: If the budget is frozen, it is hard to start a new project.

explain: 물가, 월급, 요금을 올리지도 내리지도 않고 그대로 둘 때 써요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스와 회사 소식에서 자주 나와요. 정부나 회사 같은 기관이 주어일 때가 많고, 계좌를 못 쓰게 묶을 때도 써요.
explain_en: Used when prices, pay, or fares are neither raised nor lowered but kept as they are. It appears more in news and company announcements than in daily talk. The subject is often an institution such as a government or company, and it also covers locking an account.
